en.headline: Housing chief trials water-tank cleaning robot in three estates
en.dek: The locally developed amphibious robot has been tested at Mun Tung, Hoi Ying and Lai Yiu estates and is expected to enter mass production this year.
body: Secretary for Housing Winnie Ho said a locally developed robot designed to clean public housing water tanks is already under trial at three estates and could be rolled out more widely once mass production begins this year.

The Hong Kong Construction Research Centre developed the fourth-generation machine, which can operate underwater, use high-pressure cleaning and disinfection spray, and navigate with AI assistance. Workers control it remotely from outside the confined tank, reducing the need to lower staff into the space.

Trials began in May at Mun Tung Estate, Hoi Ying Estate and Lai Yiu Estate. Ho, who operated the robot herself at Lai Yiu, said the system is safer and more efficient. The invention earlier won a gold medal at the Geneva International Exhibition of Inventions and has attracted overseas interest.

zh.headline: 洗水缸機械人三屋邨試用 何永賢冀今年量產
zh.dek: 本地研發第四代兩棲機械人已於滿東邨、海盈邨及麗瑤邨試用，可遙控操作減少密閉空間風險。
body: 房屋局局長何永賢表示，由香港智能建造研發中心研發的洗水缸機械人已在三條公共屋邨試用，期望今年內開始大量生產並逐步推展至更多屋邨。
第四代機械人具備高壓清洗、消毒噴灑及兩棲自主導航功能，可在水下傳送訊號，並以人工智能識別需加強清理位置。工友只需在缸外以遙控器操作，無需再吊入密閉空間。
試用自5月起在滿東邨、海盈邨及麗瑤邨進行。何永賢曾到麗瑤邨實地操作，形容安全高效。該發明早前於日內瓦國際發明展獲金獎，並吸引海外業界洽商。
